operator-runbook-moog-antithesis-dashboa.text: As the pipeline operator, I bring the dashboard up, keep it up, and recover when a source goes stale. I inspect the published inputs before trusting an old service observation or wallet balance. The live page, the collection loop and the push transport are described in README.md and docs/transport-design.md; this file is the hands-on companion: tokens, hosts, cutover, recovery.

token-inventory.text: Verified on the collector host (2026-10-08): read-only moog facts test-runs and moog token both work with the read env alone — no wallet paths, no being_* identity, isolated HOME. The env file needs exactly three settings: MOOG_MPFS_HOST, MOOG_TOKEN_ID, and (only moog token reads it) MOOG_GITHUB_PAT. Evidence: facts test-runs --whose cfhal exit 0 with 1486 facts; token exit 0 with the pending-request list.

action-checklist-current-state.text: Create the three status issues on this repository (one each for the oracle, agent and monitor reporters) and note their numbers as STATUS_ISSUE_ORACLE, STATUS_ISSUE_AGENT, STATUS_ISSUE_MONITOR.
Create the three status tokens (table above) plus the Pages push token and the GitHub read token.
Create the Antithesis key file and the moog read env file (provider URL and read-only settings only).

Place secret files on each host, mode 0400, owned by uid 1000: collector gets antithesis-key, gh-read, pages-push, moog-read-env under /srv/moog-antithesis-dashboard/; each reporter host gets its status-token under /srv/moog-status-reporter/.
Start the reporters through reporter/compose.yaml. The Docker group GID differs per host: run getent group docker on the host and export it as DOCKER_GID so the non-root reporter can read the socket.

Add the push hook to the monitor's script (the README one-liner: one-shot docker run of the reporter image running /app/reporter/push-verdict.sh, verdict line on stdin, token file bind-mounted read-only). Dry-run it first (REPORT_DRY_RUN=1 ./reporter/push-verdict.sh).
Flip the two GHCR packages (moog-antithesis-dashboard, moog-antithesis-dashboard-reporter) to public after the first push to main, so hosts pull without a credential.

Collector images are pinned and updated by the automatic deployment described below; reporter images stay manual. Dry-run the collector first and compare with deploy/compare-live.sh, setting all installed STATUS_ISSUE_* numbers. The legacy timer is already disabled; leave it disabled. Save the current Compose configuration and image SHA before updating; rollback restores that previous Nix-built service. Keep the existing cache volume and never run two publishers together.

Oracle and agent reporters sample every minute, publish on meaningful changes, and send a five-minute heartbeat. The collector publishes every ten minutes. The monitor hook is one-shot; its external scheduler must produce fresh reports within the fifteen-minute staleness window.

The table describes recommended credential scopes, not an attestation of every deployed token. The current collector uses existing operator tokens with broader permissions. Issues-write covers all issues in the selected repository, not one issue. The reporter's Docker socket grants privileged Engine API access despite the read-only container configuration.

recovery.text: When a card goes stale, in order: is the reporter container running (docker ps, docker logs — one failing report logs one line and the loop continues)? Is its token expired (table above)? Is the host clock in sync (more than 15 minutes behind shows stale even while reporting, more any time ahead is refused)? Can the collector reach api.github.com? What does the source error on the page banner say, and how old is last_success?
Dry-run commands (no token needed, nothing is sent or pushed):

The comparison stores its local JSON in a fresh snapshot.* directory under OUT_DIR. It compares structure and reports value differences; it ignores source freshness fields and the monitor verdict, so exit zero does not certify service health or monitor cutover. The reproduction matrix uses controlled fixtures for reporter stopping and recovery; production outage and recovery evidence must be recorded separately.

rejected-transports.text: Four designs were considered for host-to-collector status and rejected: the receiver service (a new always-on public endpoint to supervise and patch for the same outcome), pushing a git branch (the token could write gh-pages), gists (classic PAT with account-wide scope, no fine-grained option), and on-chain facts (barred: the dashboard never writes chain data). The per-issue edit won: no listening service and the smallest token blast radius.

public-wallet-configuration-and-koios-co.text: Public wallet configuration and Koios collection.

The collector reads config/wallets.json from the source repository at one commit per cycle, defaulting to main. WALLET_CONFIG_REF can pin a preview to a specific source commit. The deployed balance source supports verified preprod addresses. Provider endpoints are fixed by the application, not configurable in the JSON.

GitHub holds wallet query coordinates, not a balance issue supplied by a second publisher. Configure role, verified network, active public addresses and historical address scope in a versioned public document. Record the deployed wallet-to-role mapping evidence; never copy wallet files or private keys into the collector or repository. A testnet address alone does not determine which testnet to query.

The collector reads the document at one commit, validates its schema and scope, chooses an allowlisted Koios endpoint for that network and queries Koios directly. Antithesis follows the same direct API collection pattern for tests. The existing publication gate publishes derived wallet observations in gh-pages; inspect the snapshot there or through the dashboard. A separate wallet status publisher is not part of this design.

During recovery, distinguish a GitHub configuration failure from a Koios provider failure. The source must show its last successful query time, configured address scope and revision, network and history coverage. Rereading coordinates cannot refresh a stale balance. Pipeline and wallet cards also refuse a healthy/current label when their source is stale or its last observation is over fifteen minutes old, even if a cached boolean verdict still says OK. After address rotation, old cached observations retain the old scope and remain stale until the new scope is queried successfully. Unavailable data is never zero ADA. Complete history is never inferred from one page of transactions. Fee attribution and locked funds need transaction evidence.

mpfs-status-publication.text: As the operator, I inspect two independent MPFS cards and their GitHub feeds. Issue30 reports collector-legacy-mpfs (container mpfs-compose-mpfs-1), used by the dashboard collector. Issue37 reports moog-role-legacy-mpfs (container mpfs-mpfs-1), used by the oracle and agent. Both are legacy v1.3.0 on preprod. Matching image versions never establish that these are the same deployment. Do not substitute umpfs or use the Antithesis proxy readiness probe as MPFS evidence.

Each reporter samples every minute, publishes meaningful changes and sends a five-minute heartbeat. Container state, image, API response, readiness and slot observations are meaningful; elapsed uptime and reported_at alone are excluded from comparison. Failed writes retain the previous successful comparison and retry on the next sample. The collector reads STATUS_ISSUE_MPFS_COLLECTOR=30 and STATUS_ISSUE_MPFS_ROLES=37 separately and retains each last-good value with its own timestamp. Reports more than fifteen minutes old are stale.

The read-only GET /tokens response supplies indexerStatus. The reporter discards token records and other response fields. Synchronization is observed only when ready is boolean and both tips are nonnegative safe integer slots with the network tip at least as large as the indexer tip. Otherwise it is unmeasured. Lag is networkTip minus indexerTip against this backend's own Ogmios observation; it does not establish independently verified network freshness. API availability and a running container are displayed separately from indexer synchronization.

The legacy v1.3.0 API exposes these fields. Its block-height wording conflicts with the indexer implementation, which assigns Ogmios slot values. The dashboard therefore labels them as slots, without converting them into seconds or inventing a readiness threshold.

install-update-and-rollback.text: Use reporter/mpfs-compose.yaml with reporter/compose.yaml beside it. Provision the existing repository-scoped issue-write credential as a mounted file at /srv/moog-status-reporter/status-token, owner UID1000, mode0400; never copy it into the Compose environment. Obtain DOCKER_GID from getent group docker. Set STATUS_ISSUE_NUMBER, MPFS_SERVICE_ID and MPFS_PROBE_URL in the host-local .env. The collector reporter uses https://mpfs.plutimus.com/tokens. The role reporter uses http://127.0.0.1:3000/tokens with network_mode: host in its override. Neither private endpoint coordinates nor response bodies enter its published snapshot.

Pin a merged Nix image in deployed-image.yaml. Retain the previous override for rollback. From the reporter service directory, run these same commands for an install or an image update; the named project keeps its comparison cache.

Verify the expected service_id, container image and reported_at in that host's GitHub feed, then the corresponding public data.json source. Capture the running reporter image ID, merged revision and public observation together. A successful PATCH does not establish public dashboard publication until Pages is checked.

To roll back an update, restore the previous deployed-image.yaml and run up -d with the same project and files. To undo the first installation, run down with those files; retain the comparison cache and let the last report expire visibly. When a source is stale, inspect its own issue timestamp, reporter execution, file credential access and GitHub write outcome. Do not refresh an old verdict or manually relabel a stopped reporter as healthy.

delivery-progress.text: Oracle, agent and monitor issue reporting is deployed. MPFS has separate reporter and collector paths for the two legacy instances; production evidence is attached to its delivery ticket. Current Koios balance collection and the ADA account cards are implemented; their installation uses the same collector image and publication path. Configure its GitHub read access to the source repository. Expense history, locked-fund accounting and provider observations bound to an exact chain point remain open. The funds tickets retain balance and historical accounting as distinct acceptance requirements. See the system design and issues MPFS, agent/oracle and requester.

monitor-publication-and-snapshot-api.text: The existing Antithesis freshness producer publishes a sanitized verdict through the Nix reporter image to status issue34. Its production wrapper preserves the existing notification behavior, publishes failure as a generic verdict and retains a five-minute producer interval. File-mounted status credentials stay on the producing host. The collector reads STATUS_ISSUE_MONITOR=34; inspect the issue timestamp and next producer execution when recovering a stale source.

On NixOS the wrapper explicitly invokes /run/wrappers/bin/sudo for the Docker command: the service PATH excludes the setuid wrapper directory. A non-setuid sudo from the system profile fails in the scheduled service even when an interactive operator invocation succeeds. Production receipt records this live boundary check. Host unit drop-ins must be retained when rebuilding NixOS.

Swagger UI lives at swagger.html beside openapi.json and data.json. The schema describes the public snapshot, not the external provider APIs. Try it out reads the same directory snapshot. CDN assets are version-pinned with integrity hashes; the specification is not sent to an external validation service. Schema CI checks recorded actual and unavailable snapshots and refuses malformed claims.

automatic-collector-deployment.text: As a dashboard maintainer, I merge a checked change and the running collector and public page update without manual deployment commands. The collector host polls GitHub, and one Nix-packaged Babashka command does everything:

update deploys only the current head of main, and only when its complete push CI run succeeded: every job is successful or skipped, and the collector image and reproduction jobs are both successful. Pull request runs, failed runs, pending runs and an older revision are refused with the reason printed and recorded. Image publication alone is not enough, because it precedes the final reproduction job. The head is read again after the image is pulled; if main moved, nothing deploys.

The selected image is pulled by commit tag, bound to its registry digest, and pinned in deployed-image.yaml as repository:tag@sha256:digest. If the tag ever resolves to another digest, the update is refused. Only the collector service is recreated, with the existing compose.yaml, mounts, cache volume, secrets and environment untouched. Another container of the collector image outside the project, or a second running update, blocks the rollout. Repeating the same revision changes nothing.

The diagram shows the three verdicts. A refused revision never reaches the collector. A collector that fails to start, or whose first cycle does not publish a new valid snapshot, gets the previous pinned override restored, and the failure is recorded in the state directory. A healthy collector whose page has not caught up is reported on its own, without a rollback and without touching GitHub Pages.

Exit codes are 0 deployed or already current, 1 failed and rolled back, 2 refused, 3 CI still running, 4 Pages pending, 5 Pages build failed. A revision that failed is not retried until update --retry. Pages pending or failed is re-observed on the next update without redeploying; the command never deletes, resets or recreates Pages.

install-on-the-collector-host.text: The unit pair is in deploy/systemd/. Copy both files to /etc/systemd/system/, set User and the three paths, then enable the timer:

The command needs docker with the Compose plugin on PATH, bb, gh and curl (the package supplies the last three). The GitHub token is the existing read file and reaches the command as a credential file; it needs Actions, contents and Pages read access. It is never an argument, never logged, and no token or Docker socket enters the collector container. State lives in deploy-state/ beside the stack: state.json, history.jsonl, the previous override and bindings.json. The first update after installation recreates the collector once to move from a tag pin to a digest pin.

status-and-rollback.text: status prints the pinned image, the running container, the deployed revision, collector and Pages health, the previous pin and the last failure. rollback restores the previous pin and waits for it to run; it does nothing when no previous pin is recorded. If a rollback itself fails, history.jsonl records rollback-failed and the unit stays failed: restore deploy-state/previous-override.yaml over deployed-image.yaml by hand and run docker compose up -d.

Timeouts are DEPLOY_STARTUP_SECONDS, DEPLOY_SNAPSHOT_SECONDS and DEPLOY_PAGES_SECONDS. The deploy-controls check runs the packaged command against disposable fixtures for every refusal, both rollback causes, Pages pending and failure, and serialization.
